drills.title: Sharks and Fishes
drills.objective: Change direction into space.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Runners cross between end lines; one or two sharks tag them. Tagged runners become sharks next round. Reset until all have crossed.
drills.coaching: Look up; change pace; avoid bunching. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.regression: Widen area or use one shark.
drills.progression: Carry a ball in two hands.
drills.questions: Where was the gap before you started? What changed when the shark moved?
drills.notes: Watch whether the quieter runners reach the line as often as the fastest. Give them a wider starting gap if needed.

drills.title: Rats and Rabbits
drills.objective: React and accelerate.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Pair players on two parallel lines, each facing their own safety line. Call one team; they run to safety while partners pursue for a light tag. Reset.
drills.coaching: React to the call; leave room to decelerate. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.regression: Use a visual signal and walking.
drills.progression: Mix visual and verbal cues.
drills.questions: What helped you react to the call? How did you slow down at the end?
drills.notes: Call both teams equally. Leave a clear run-off beyond each safety line; switch partners regularly.

frames.name: Set up · Rats and Rabbits
frames.notes: Two pairs start in parallel lanes. The blue and red cones mark separate safety lines; allow clear run-off outside both.

frames.name: Coach calls RATS
frames.notes: The coach calls RATS: R1 and R2 run towards the blue safety line. H1 and H2 react, but no physical contact is allowed.

frames.name: Light tag before the line
frames.notes: The nearest chaser closes under control for an agreed light tag. Do not grab, push or run through the safety line.

frames.name: Swap the call · RABBITS
frames.notes: Reset to the centre and switch who runs to safety. Alternate the calls fairly so both teams practise reacting and chasing.

drills.title: Rob the Nest
drills.objective: Scan and change direction.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.equipment: 5 hoops or marked nests, 8 balls, cones
drills.instructions: Place balls at centre with teams at corner nests. One runner per team collects one ball each trip; then tag the next teammate. No stealing from hands.
drills.coaching: Look up at centre; carry securely. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.progression: Allow taking one unattended ball from another nest.
drills.questions: Which nest has the clearest route? Where will you look before picking up the ball?
drills.notes: One child runs per team; the rest wait behind their nest. Count balls at the end instead of encouraging children to wrestle for them.

frames.name: Set up · Rob the Nest
frames.notes: One runner per team starts at a time. The central balls are loose; neither team takes a ball from another player's hands.

frames.name: One runner per team
frames.notes: A1 and D1 run separately to the centre. A2 and D2 wait behind their nests; nobody reaches across an opponent.

frames.name: Collect one ball each
frames.notes: Each runner takes just one ball from the centre, stays on feet and turns into their own clear return lane.

frames.name: Return to the nests
frames.notes: Return the balls to your team's nest. Next runners wait for a clear handover before starting their turn.

drills.title: Animal Walks Relay
drills.objective: Develop coordination and balance.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Set short parallel lanes. Children explore bear crawls and other comfortable animal movements, then return walking. Keep bouts short.
drills.coaching: Move with control; stop if uncomfortable. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.progression: Combine two movement patterns.
drills.questions: Which movement is easiest to control? Can you keep the same balance when you change direction?
drills.notes: Let children choose a comfortable movement. This is coordination practice, not a race or fitness punishment.

drills.title: Dog and Bone
drills.objective: React and find an escape route.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Number two teams facing a loose central ball. Call a number from each; first to collect the ball tries to return behind their line before a light tag. No diving for the ball.
drills.coaching: Approach under control; scan before turning. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.regression: Call one player with no opponent.
drills.progression: Call two numbers and allow a support pass.
drills.questions: Could you collect the ball without running into your opponent? Where was your safest way out?
drills.notes: Call one pair at a time initially. If two arrive together, stop and reset rather than letting them dive at the ball.

frames.name: Set up · Dog and Bone

frames.name: A1 collects · D1 slows

frames.name: Return safely behind line
frames.notes: A1 turns and returns to the blue home line, while D1 chases under control. If close enough, use only an agreed light touch.

drills.title: Mirror Movement
drills.objective: Track direction without crossing feet unnecessarily.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.players: 2 per group
drills.instructions: Partners face each other with a safe gap; leader shuffles and changes direction for 10–15 seconds. Follower mirrors without touching; swap.
drills.coaching: Stay balanced; watch torso and hips. Coach observation: Watch the first shared step and the gap between adjacent defenders; praise a clear call before a rush.
drills.progression: Add forward and backward movement.
drills.questions: What tells you your partner is about to change direction? How can you stay balanced?
drills.notes: Keep the partners facing one another and give each pair room. Change leader after a short bout.

drills.title: Balance Challenge
drills.objective: Develop single-leg control.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.players: Any
drills.instructions: In personal spaces, stand on one leg briefly, reach or receive a gentle pass, then switch. Keep movements comfortable.
drills.coaching: Soft knee; steady trunk; eyes up. When practising directional rugby, keep receivers behind the ball and pass sideways or backwards.
drills.progression: Add a small reach or gentle catch.
drills.questions: What helps you stay steady? Can you catch without putting your other foot down?
drills.notes: Offer a wall-side or two-foot version if needed. Count quality repetitions rather than how long someone can endure.

drills.instructions: Use separated personal spaces; jump a short distance and hold a stable landing before resetting. Low repetitions and no fatigue challenge.

drills.questions: What does a quiet landing feel like? Can you hold your landing for two seconds?
drills.notes: Use low, short jumps on a suitable surface; a stable landing matters more than distance.

drills.title: Passing Circle
drills.objective: Present hands and catch cleanly.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Space children in a circle. Pass to a teammate who calls and shows hands. Follow with a moving version.
drills.coaching: Hands ready; look at target; follow through. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace.
drills.progression: Introduce a second ball if spacing allows.
drills.questions: When should your hands be ready? How can you let your teammate know you want the ball?
drills.notes: Non-directional handling circle: catching, calling and showing hands. There is deliberately no attacking try line. This exercise is NOT a legal forward-pass option in match play; follow with a directional backward passing activity.

drills.title: Five Pass Game
drills.objective: Move into a passing lane.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Two teams compete for five completed sideways or backward passes without contact. Blue attacks towards the top of the diagram and orange towards the opposite end. Support moves behind the carrier; a drop, interception or forward pass changes possession. Reset the count on a turnover.
drills.coaching: Move after passing, call early and stay behind the ball. Do not force a pass to a teammate ahead of the carrier.
drills.progression: Return to directional rugby passing laws.
drills.questions: Where can you move so the passer can see you? What should you do after passing?
drills.notes: This directional version counts legal passes rather than any-direction throws. Reset or reverse the attack when possession changes; the animation shows the first three passes.

frames.name: Create lane

frames.name: Continue

drills.title: L-shaped Passing
drills.objective: Catch while moving and realign.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Mark an L-shaped route. A runner receives from a feeder near the turn and passes to a waiting teammate after changing direction. Rotate roles.
drills.coaching: Give a target; adjust pace; pass to space. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace.
drills.progression: Add a passive defender at the turn.
drills.questions: How can A1 prepare to catch before reaching the corner? When should A3 call?
drills.notes: An L-shaped unopposed handling exercise: the running direction changes at the corner, so it does not represent a fixed rugby attack direction. Re-check the legal backward pass before transferring this skill into a game.

frames.name: Set up the L
frames.notes: The L-turn handling pattern now has A3 waiting behind A1's turn, so the eventual pass can travel backwards when the runner turns upfield.

frames.name: Receive on the move
frames.notes: A1 runs to the turn; hands ready before the feed.

frames.name: Turn and pass
frames.notes: A1 turns and passes backwards to A3, whose position remains behind the current ball carrier. Keep a clear receiving lane and rotate the feeder and runner.

drills.title: Passing Gauntlet
drills.objective: Pass accurately while moving.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.players: One runner and three feeders per lane; rotate roles.
drills.instructions: Place feeders at successive stations. Runners collect a pass from behind or level with the feeder, move just beyond them and return the ball sideways or backwards. Rotate feeders often.
drills.coaching: Keep eyes up; turn hands toward ball; avoid rushing. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace.
drills.progression: Vary distance and timing of feeds.
drills.questions: When should the feeder release the ball? Can the runner catch without stopping?
drills.notes: Three separate balls are used. The runner moves past each feeder before returning the ball; keep the next runner back until the lane is clear. Feeders are stationary handling partners, not advancing teammates.

frames.name: Passing stations
frames.notes: One runner starts behind the first station. Feeders F1–F3 each have a ball and stay outside the running channel.

frames.name: Receive at station 1
frames.notes: Feeder 1 passes as A1 reaches the station. Runner shows hands and catches without stopping.

frames.name: Return and continue 1
frames.notes: A1 moves just beyond the feeder, then returns the ball sideways or backwards. Continue to the next station after the ball has gone.

frames.name: Receive at station 2
frames.notes: Feeder 2 passes as A1 reaches the station. Runner shows hands and catches without stopping.

frames.name: Return and continue 2
frames.notes: A1 moves just beyond the feeder, then returns the ball sideways or backwards. Continue to the next station after the ball has gone.

frames.name: Return and continue 3

drills.title: Diamond Passing
drills.objective: Create useful support angles.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Start four players in a diamond; pass to a moving adjacent player and follow into the vacated position. Reset if spacing collapses.
drills.coaching: Call early; move as ball travels; maintain distance. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace.
drills.progression: Add a roaming passive defender.
drills.questions: When can the passer follow? How much space should the next receiver leave?
drills.notes: Non-directional diamond handling/catch-and-follow: no attacking end. Some passes would be forward if you treated the top of the diagram as the opposition try line. Use this only for ball-handling practice; use the directional continuous-passing lesson to teach legal match passes.

frames.name: Pass A1 → A2

frames.name: Pass A3 → A4

frames.name: Pass A4 → A1

drills.title: Two-ball End Ball
drills.objective: Scan more than one passing option.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Use two marked scoring zones. Teams score by passing to a teammate inside a zone. Begin with one ball before introducing the second, with clear possession rules. This is a deliberately modified, non-match End Ball game: scoring-zone passes may travel forwards under the game's own rules. Explain that the same pass is illegal in normal rugby; for rugby-law practice, position the receiving player level with or behind the ball carrier instead.
drills.coaching: Scan before receiving; communicate which ball is live. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace. Distinguish the modified End Ball scoring rule from a legal rugby pass: do not present a forward scoring-zone pass as a match example.
drills.progression: Add a second scoring zone per end.
drills.questions: Which ball are you offering for? How do you avoid two receivers chasing the same pass?
drills.notes: Teach the one-ball game first. Only add the second ball when players can communicate and scan reliably. This is a modified handling game without a fixed match attack direction. For directional rugby practice, require sideways or backward passes.

frames.name: Set up · Two-ball End Ball
frames.notes: Two marked scoring zones. Start with a single active ball; the second is deliberately parked until the players are ready.

frames.name: Begin with one active ball
frames.notes: First practise with b1 only. A1 looks up while A2 moves into the far scoring lane. b2 remains inactive on the ground.

frames.name: Pass to the scoring zone
frames.notes: Modified End Ball game (NOT normal rugby laws): A1 passes into the scoring zone to A2 ahead. For a rugby-law version, keep the receiver behind the carrier and award points for a completed backwards pass instead.

frames.name: Add the second ball only when ready
frames.notes: After everyone understands one-ball scoring, the coach may activate the second ball. D2 collects it from a safe separate position; avoid two-ball confusion.

drills.title: Continuous Passing
drills.objective: Receive while advancing.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Small lines advance together and pass laterally or backwards; rotate the starter and running direction, then repeat.
drills.coaching: Keep depth; move onto the pass; avoid drifting together. Coach observation: Look for visible hands and an early receiver call before the ball travels; prioritise completed catches over pace.
drills.progression: Add a defender to force a choice.
drills.questions: How do you stay available while the line advances? What happens if everyone runs level?
drills.notes: Four runners are shown. Keep the receiving line staggered, and rotate the first carrier rather than always starting on one side.

drills.title: 2 vs 1 · Draw and pass
drills.objective: Exploit a two-on-one advantage.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.players: 3 per group
drills.instructions: Two attackers advance against a touch defender. The carrier chooses to pass or run based on the defender. Swap roles after each short attempt.
drills.coaching: Carry in two hands; hold width; pass before the space closes. Coach observation: Freeze the decision moment: ask the carrier to name the defender's movement, then the available support lane.
drills.progression: Add a recovering defender.
drills.questions: Has the defender committed to the carrier? Is the pass really needed?
drills.notes: Pause at the decision diamond. The gold route is an alternative to discuss, not an automatically played branch. Let the carrier make the choice in practice.

drills.objective: Find gaps and evade.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Runners try to cross a grid without light tags from the octopus. Tagged runners join the middle on the next round. Keep movement controlled.
drills.coaching: Run into free space; change speed; avoid collision. Coach observation: Watch for scanning and safe deceleration; reward control rather than the fastest run.
drills.progression: Runners carry rugby balls.
drills.questions: Where is the space between taggers? When can you change pace?
drills.notes: Tagged children join the middle on the next crossing. Keep enough clear space for the group rather than making a crowded wall of taggers.

drills.title: 1v1 Channel
drills.objective: Beat a defender in a small space.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.

drills.progression: Narrow slightly or vary start positions.
drills.questions: Which side of the defender is open? Can you change direction without losing control?
drills.notes: Use short repetitions and rotate the defending role. Reward a good decision even when the tagger catches the runner.

drills.title: Four-goal Touch
drills.objective: Scan beyond the immediate defender.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.instructions: Four marked gates serve as scoring targets in a multidirectional touch game. Agree turnover rules and reset after a point.

drills.title: U10 Breakdown · Tackle, Present, Support and Play
drills.objective: Recognise the sequence from tackle to a ball available to play, with one arriving support player each side.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Rehearse the sequence without contact first.
drills.players: 3 attackers and 3 defenders; rotate carrier, tackler and support roles.
drills.instructions: Walk through A1's tackle, D1's release and the presentation. A2 arrives first; D2 then joins from the opposite side. Keep A3 and D3 out of the ruck. When the ball is available, A3 collects and passes to A2 after A2 has disengaged.
drills.coaching: Release and present without delay. The arriving players enter from their own side and remain on their feet. Once the ball is available, move it away rather than sending in another player.
drills.regression: Use a stationary ball and walk to the positions without binding or tackling.
drills.progression: Change which side arrives first in a no-contact walk-through; ask players to find the next receiver.
drills.questions: Why does A3 wait outside the ruck? When can A2 become a receiver again?
drills.notes: Shows a single tackle followed by one additional player from each team. The ruck is a positional diagram, not instruction in clearing out.

drills.objective: Demonstrate the sequence of a tackle, ball presentation, defender arriving with a contact shield and attacking support arriving from their own side.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Use a passive shield as a position marker; do not charge into a shield holder or teach a clearout from the animation.
drills.players: 3 attackers and 3 defenders; D2 holds the passive shield.

drills.title: U10 · Offload to support
drills.objective: Keep the ball alive by passing backwards to a supporting teammate before the carrier is brought to ground.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration: no opponent or tackle is shown. Use controlled pace and adequate space; contact practice requires qualified supervision.
drills.players: A1 carrier and A2 tracking support. Two-player non-contact passing practice.
drills.instructions: In a short channel, A1 jogs forward with the ball while A2 tracks behind and slightly to one side. A1 checks support is available, then passes backwards before a tackle. A2 catches and continues forward. Repeat from both sides before introducing passive touch pressure.
drills.coaching: A1 looks before releasing; A2 stays behind the ball and communicates early. Catch first, then accelerate. Don't force the pass when the support is not there.
drills.regression: Stationary two-handed pass to a nearby support player.
drills.progression: Add a touch defender to give A1 a carry-or-pass decision.
drills.questions: Where is A2 when the ball is released? Can A2 catch while moving? When should A1 keep the ball?
drills.notes: This shows just the offload pass. It does not teach a pass from the ground or contact technique.
drills.provenance: Original schematic demonstration · research-informed

drills.title: U10 · Free pass restart
drills.objective: See where a U10 free pass is taken after touch, the defenders' seven-metre retreat and when players can move.
drills.safety: No charging onto the pass or rushing an unready receiver. Walk through the restart initially.
drills.players: A1 free-pass taker, A2 receiver, D1 and D2 retreating defenders.
drills.equipment: Rugby ball, boundary cones and a tape measure.
drills.instructions: After touch, mark the free pass 5 m inside the touchline. A1 stays at the mark, A2 waits behind and defenders D1 and D2 retreat at least 7 m. Once the referee calls Play, A1 passes backwards. Nobody runs before the ball is passed.
drills.coaching: Measure the restart mark and the seven-metre retreat rather than estimating. A1 holds the ball in two hands and passes backwards; everyone waits until that pass has been made.
drills.regression: Two stationary players and cones to show the retreat line.
drills.progression: Add defenders behind the marked line, then continue a touch game after the pass.
drills.questions: Where is the free-pass mark after touch? Have both defenders retired seven metres? Exactly when can A2 and the defenders run?
drills.notes: The 2026–27 U10 summary specifies a 7 m retreat and a restart 5 m in from touch where applicable. The two-player diagram does not draw the defending line.
drills.provenance: Original schematic demonstration · research-informed

drills.progression: Add a passive defending line at the correct retreat distance once the coach has checked the law.

drills.title: U12 · Grubber · kick and collect

drills.objective: Recognise a try as grounding the ball in the opponents' in-goal area.

drills.instructions: Mark a try line and an in-goal area with clear run-off. A1 approaches at walking pace and grounds the ball under control; A2 follows with space. Repeat from a different angle.
drills.coaching: Keep control of the ball and ground it over or on the try line. The referee decides whether a try has been scored.
drills.regression: Start stationary at the marked line.
drills.progression: Approach from a different angle with passive, non-contact opposition.
drills.questions: Where does the ball need to be grounded? Why do we leave room beyond the line?

drills.title: U14 · Goal kick · attempt
drills.objective: Identify the place-kicker's starting position and the intended goal line.

drills.instructions: Set the ball on a tee at an agreed mark. Give the kicker an unobstructed approach. Aim towards the target; wait until the area is clear before retrieving the ball.

drills.title: U10 · Tracking a rolling tackle donut
drills.objective: Track a moving training pad and select a controlled interception point.
drills.players: One active tackler at a time; coach controls roll and reset.
drills.equipment: One age-appropriate tackle donut and two cones.
drills.instructions: Walk through the approach, then roll slowly in a clear lane. Intercept before the end marker; reset each turn.
drills.coaching: Eyes up, adjust feet, remain balanced. Use club-approved progressive tackle instruction. Finish the tracking approach at the trailing side of the rolling pad, with head placement checked by the coach.
drills.safety: Qualified coach supervision. Follow equipment instructions; keep others clear. No head-first dives or high-speed pursuit.
drills.progression: Vary approach angle at controlled speed.
drills.questions: Where will the pad be when you arrive?
drills.notes: The pad's stop is illustrated, not calculated from collision forces. Stand it upright and reset the lane between attempts.

drills.title: U10 · Read the defender — tackle or offload
drills.objective: Recognise when to carry into space, keep possession through contact or pass to a teammate in support. Compare demonstrated and alternative actions.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Use a passive shield as a position marker; do not charge into a shield holder or teach a clearout from the animation.
drills.players: 3 attackers, 3 defenders; D2 marks the defending arrival with a passive shield.
drills.equipment: Rugby ball, cones and a contact shield.
drills.instructions: Pause the first approach and ask A1 to choose an open carry or an available backward offload. The shown outcome continues to a tackle and presentation, then follows the shield-marked defender-first breakdown. A3 plays away; rotate the shield holder.
drills.coaching: Scan before contact. If a safe pass is not available, do not force it. Release and present immediately after grounding; support arrives from its own side and stays on its feet. Keep other players clear.
drills.regression: Show the alternatives without contact, using a cone instead of a shield.
drills.progression: Vary the support runner's starting position and let the carrier choose during touch practice.
drills.questions: Where is the space? Is support available for a safe backwards offload? When should the carrier secure the ball instead?

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 ruck entry

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 offside at the ruck

drills.title: React to the carrier · two outcomes
drills.players: 5 defenders in a line, 1 attacking runner, 1 coach/feeder
drills.equipment: 1 ball, 4 cones. Touch only for coach-carry option.
drills.objective: Defenders take a coordinated step forward on a signal, read the ball carrier, then communicate and close the selected channel together.
drills.instructions: Start with D1–D5 in one line. The ball is on the ground just in front of the coach. One attacker waits slightly behind and to the other side. On the coach’s whistle, the entire defensive line takes a few steps forward. Outcome A: coach picks up and carries towards one channel; D2 and D3 close and make controlled touch. Outcome B: coach picks up and passes backwards to the runner; D4 and D5 track and complete a controlled tackle. Alternate outcomes without telling the defenders which is coming; reset to the same setup each time.
drills.coaching: Keep spacing and communicate. Scan before advancing; step up at the same time. The two nearest defenders work together while the rest stay in line. The attacker should look up, find space and never throw a forward pass.
drills.safety: Do not ask U10 children to tackle an adult coach in live contact. The coach-carry version is touch only; for live contact use an age-matched carrier instead. For the runner-tackle option, a qualified coach must control speed, contact height below the base of the sternum, safe head position and gradual progression. Do not allow uncontrolled double hits. Check RFU age-grade regulations and club safeguarding policy.
drills.regression: Walking pace, tell defenders which option is coming, and use touch for both outcomes.
drills.progression: Keep the choice hidden until the signal and let attackers vary their channels.
drills.questions: Who called the carrier first? Did your spacing hold when two defenders closed the gap? Could you identify the threat before the pass? Was the pass backwards?
drills.notes: Worked example of a genuine two-outcome drill. Choose A/B in the editor or read-only player. Movies contain labelled A and B chapters; coaching sheets cover both.

drills.title: Hold the line · Carry or pass?
drills.objective: Defenders move together, scan for the ball carrier and close the right channel without losing the line. The attack has a genuine choice: the coach carries, or passes backwards to A1.
drills.safety: U10 activity: begin with touch for both outcomes. Never ask children to tackle an adult coach. The adult-carry outcome is always a two-hand touch demonstration. If practising the A1 tackle, use only age-matched participants with an appropriately qualified coach, a progressive tackle warm-up, controlled speed and the current RFU tackle-height requirement. drills.players: Six defenders (D1–D6), one support attacker (A1), one coach/ball feeder. Start with all six defenders across the same line. The coach and A1 are behind them, with A1 slightly deeper to receive.
drills.equipment: One rugby ball and four cones to mark an 11 × 20 m working area. No contact pads are required for the touch version.
drills.instructions:
Set up D1–D6 in a connected defensive line. The ball begins on the ground by the coach; A1 waits deeper and to the opposite side. On the whistle, defenders take a few controlled steps forward together. The coach runs towards the line and a decision is reached. PAUSE: choose A or B.
A — Carry: the coach keeps the ball and runs into the near-side channel. D1 and D2 close the space and make a two-hand TOUCH on the adult coach. Stop and reset.
B — Pass: the coach passes backwards to A1. D4 tracks A1 into the outside channel and completes a controlled tackle; D5 closes the space as cover, not as a simultaneous second tackler. A1 releases and presents the ball. Reset to the same start after either option.
Try both outcomes. For the players, avoid announcing which option the coach will choose until the defenders have started moving.
drills.coaching:
DEFENCE — Go together on GO, not six separate sprints. Look across the line and talk: 'UP', 'BALL', 'MY SIDE'. Shorten steps as the carrier approaches. The closest player tracks the hips; the next defender covers the space beside them. Everyone else stays connected and watches for the pass.
ATTACK — Pick up securely, eyes up and choose space. When passing, keep A1 behind the carrier and send the ball backwards. A1 catches before accelerating; keep the ball available after a legal tackle.
Keep the tempo modest. One good read and one good call are more valuable than a big collision.
drills.regression: First walk it through with defenders knowing the option. Use two-hand touch on every carrier, keep the pass simple and allow a verbal pause so the defenders can identify their responsibilities.
drills.progression: Do not reveal A or B until the coach reaches the decision. Vary the channel, move the receiving attacker to a new starting position (still behind for the pass), or shorten the time defenders have to communicate. Increase pace only after the defensive line stays organised; contact is a separate technical progression.
drills.questions: Who noticed the ball changing hands first? Did all six defenders move up together? Which two players were responsible for the channel, and who kept the line connected? Was the pass backwards? Could you stop the run with safe positioning rather than a rushed hit?
drills.notes: This drill contains two real playable outcomes after a shared whistle and defensive advance. Playback stops at the diamond. Choose A or B and the animation continues with different ball possession and defender reactions. The standard video export plays A and B in labelled chapters; the coaching sheet shows both. The illustrations are coach-authored examples, not automatic tactical predictions or official RFU material.

branching.question: Ball carrier's choice: carry into the gap or pass to A1?

choices.label: Coach carries · D1 and D2 close for touch

frames.name: A1 · Carry into the near-side channel
frames.notes: Coach keeps the ball and accelerates through the near-side gap. D1 calls the carrier, D2 covers the inside, and the other defenders remain connected. D1 and D2 stop the adult coach with two-hand touch only.

frames.name: A2 · Two-hand touch · stop and reset
frames.notes: Freeze when D1 and D2 have closed the channel. Count the touch; do not make a live tackle on the adult. Ask who called the ball and whether the rest of the line stayed connected.

choices.explanation: The coach keeps the ball and carries into the inside channel. The nearest two defenders close the gap and finish with two-hand touch. Children must not tackle an adult coach.
choices.watchFor: D2 and D3 communicate, close space without diving in and hold the inside. The other defenders keep their channels rather than chasing the coach.

choices.label: Coach passes · A1 attacks D4's channel

frames.name: B1 · Backwards pass to A1
frames.notes: Coach passes backwards across to A1, who stays deeper until the ball arrives. D4 calls the receiver; D5 covers the neighbouring channel while the remaining defenders stay connected.

frames.name: B2 · A1 attacks; D4 tackles
frames.notes: A1 receives, looks up and carries into the outside channel. D4 tracks A1, shortens steps and makes the controlled tackle using safe head placement and a wrap. D5 closes the adjacent gap as cover; D5 does not join the tackle.

frames.name: B3 · Release and present
frames.notes: D4 releases and gets back to feet. A1 goes to ground safely, releases and presents the ball away from pressure. D5 stays on feet and does not dive into the contact area. Reset the players and repeat with the other outcome.

choices.explanation: The coach passes backwards to A1. The outside defenders track the new ball carrier, with one controlled age-matched tackler and a covering defender in the demonstration.
choices.watchFor: Watch the backward pass, D4's approach to the ball carrier and D5's covering position. The tackle must be controlled and supervised by a qualified coach.

branching.context: The first movement is the same in both cases: the defensive line advances together on the whistle. The choice comes when the ball is played. Defenders must identify the actual carrier before changing their shape.
branching.watchFor: Look at the first two steps: are all six defenders moving on the same cue, with their spacing intact? Then watch which defenders communicate and adjust to the carrier.

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 backward or forward pass?
drills.objective: Recognise an illegal forward passing option and create a legal supporting line.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Pause while A2 is ahead of A1 and ask if a pass to that position would be legal. Move A2 deeper; then play the legal backward pass and follow-up run.
drills.coaching: The direction the ball is thrown matters, not simply the receiver's final position. Supporters give the carrier a backwards or sideways passing option.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: May A1 throw forward to A2? Where must A2 go to help? What changes after the catch?
drills.notes: The forward option is deliberately NOT animated as a completed pass. Only the legal alternative is played.
drills.provenance: U10 RFU Regulation 15 (2026–27) · coaching demonstration

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: PAUSE · receiver ahead
frames.notes: A2 is ahead. A1 must NOT throw the ball forward.

frames.name: Offer depth
frames.notes: A2 drops behind A1 to provide a legal option.

frames.name: Pass backwards
frames.notes: The ball moves from A1 towards A2, behind the line of the carrier's advance. Ask the children to trace the ball's direction.

frames.name: Run after receiving
frames.notes: After securing the backward pass, A2 may accelerate forward into space with their teammates following.

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 what is a knock-on?
drills.objective: Recognise a ball knocked forward and know that play stops for a scrum.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Watch A1 lose the ball towards the opposition try line. Pause and check that it touches the ground before A1 can recover it. Then award the scrum.
drills.coaching: A knock forward happens here because the loose ball goes forward and reaches the ground before A1 regains it. U10 uses an uncontested three-player scrum for this infringement.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Which way did the ball go? Did A1 catch it before the ground? Why does the referee stop play?
drills.notes: Only the whistle and scrum award are shown here; the scrum formation is in the dedicated U10 lesson.

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Carrier advances
frames.notes: A1 advances towards D1. Ask the children to watch both the player's hands and the direction of the ball.

frames.name: Ball lost forward
frames.notes: The ball is lost forwards, not intentionally passed to a teammate.

frames.name: PAUSE · knock-on
frames.notes: The referee stops play. Discuss why the direction matters.

frames.name: Scrum awarded · see next lesson

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 run in support
drills.objective: Stay behind the ball and offer an available backward pass.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Pause with A2 deeper and wider than A1. Ask where the pass can go, then play the backward pass and let A2 straighten after receiving.
drills.coaching: Support keeps useful width, depth and eyes on the ball carrier. A2 must not sprint in front of the ball and remove the passing option.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Is A2 behind the ball? Is the passing lane clear? What should A2 do after the catch?
drills.notes: The support line is more important than the speed: replay it at half speed and discuss the position.

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Carry into space
frames.notes: A1 runs into a channel; A2 stays wider and deeper to support a backward pass.

frames.name: PAUSE · give a passing option
frames.notes: PAUSE: A2 is behind A1 and far enough outside to provide a clear passing target.

frames.name: Pass to support
frames.notes: A1 passes backwards into A2's hands. Explain how the support line made that possible.

frames.name: Carry after the catch
frames.notes: A2 moves forward only after receiving.

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 free pass and seven-metre retreat
drills.objective: Identify the free-pass mark, retreat seven metres and pass before running.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Stop at the free-pass mark. Measure the seven-metre retreat with cones, then restart with a pass. Nobody should begin running before the pass.
drills.coaching: At U10 the ball starts in both hands, the opponents retire at least seven metres, and the passer passes backwards rather than tapping or running first.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Which team gets the free pass? Where must defenders wait? When may everyone begin to run?
drills.notes: The marked 7 m retreat line is measured from the free-pass position. Defenders wait on their own side of that line until the pass starts play; this is an understanding exercise, not a physical restart technique lesson.

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Free pass awarded
frames.notes: STOP: identify the mark and the team restarting.

frames.name: Retreat 7 m
frames.notes: D1 and D2 step back. Use an actual 7 m measurement in practice.

frames.name: Pass before running
frames.notes: A1 restarts with a backward pass to A2. The other players must not charge ahead before the pass.

frames.name: Play continues
frames.notes: A2 moves into the space only after receiving the restart pass; D1 and D2 can then defend.

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 the uncontested three-player scrum
drills.objective: Understand the U10 scrum, straight feed and pass-away requirement.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Count three players per team. Stop at the scrum shape, then play the uncontested feed, collection and pass away. Use a qualified coach for real engagement.
drills.coaching: The U10 scrum has three players on each side and no pushing. The putting-in side is allowed the age-grade strike; the scrum half must pass the ball out rather than run.
drills.safety: Scrum engagement, binding and body position require qualified age-grade coaching; do not rehearse them from the screen.
drills.regression: Use six cones and a stationary ball to identify roles; no physical engagement.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: How many players form the scrum? Is pushing allowed? Who feeds? What must the scrum half do with the ball?
drills.notes: Three players per side, Crouch–Bind–Set, no pushing; the putting-in scrum-half passes away. The measured 5 m guide is for the attacking backs, not the scrum-half. The graphic is not a scrum contact-technique demonstration.

frames.name: Crouch · Bind · Set
frames.notes: PAUSE: three players each side. No pushing.

frames.name: Feed into tunnel
frames.notes: The putting-in nine feeds from the side into the middle of the tunnel. The diagram does not demonstrate a live scrum technique.

frames.name: Ball moves to rear

frames.name: Nine collects
frames.notes: A9 collects, but must not run with it.

frames.name: Nine passes away

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 held upright · when is it a maul?
drills.objective: Distinguish a maul from a tackle/ruck and show the U10 two-per-side limit.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Freeze while A1 is still on their feet. Add A2 and D2 and identify the small maul. Ask who stays outside before the ball is played away.
drills.coaching: A maul has the ball carrier still upright, with bound teammates and opponents. This U10 picture is limited to two participants on each side; A3 stays out.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Is A1 on the ground? Has a tackle happened? Who belongs in the maul and who waits?
drills.notes: An upright maul is not a ruck. No physical ripping, binding or live contact is taught by this drawing.
drills.provenance: U10 RFU Regulation 15 (2026–27) · coaching demonstration
drills.review: Club coach to verify age-grade interpretation before training

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Held upright
frames.notes: A1 remains standing, with D1 in contact. No ground tackle.

frames.name: Maul · two per side
frames.notes: PAUSE: A1/A2 and D1/D2 make up the maul; A3 waits.

frames.name: Play the ball away
frames.notes: A1 passes backwards to A3. No real rip is being taught.

frames.name: Next phase
frames.notes: A3 carries into the space after the catch.

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 when is a try scored?
drills.objective: Explain that a try requires controlled grounding, not merely crossing a line.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Use the marked try line and shaded in-goal strip. Pause after A1 has crossed while still holding the ball; then show it grounded beyond the line.
drills.coaching: Crossing the line with the ball is not enough. A try requires the attacking team to ground it in the opposition in-goal. The referee judges the grounding.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Where is the try line? Is crossing while carrying already a try? What changes when the ball touches the ground?
drills.notes: The marked goal line is at y=100 on this teaching pitch. The ball grounds at y=70, inside the shaded in-goal strip.

frames.name: Approach try line

frames.name: Cross carrying the ball

frames.name: Ground the ball

frames.name: Explain why

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 held up in goal · no try
drills.objective: Know that held-up is not a try and that U10 restarts with an attacking five-metre scrum.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Freeze with A1 beyond the marked try line, holding the ball off the ground. Then point to the attacking scrum mark five metres back in the field.
drills.coaching: Held up in-goal without grounding is not a try. For U10 the restart is an attacking five-metre uncontested scrum, explained in a separate lesson.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: Did the ball touch the ground? Is it a try? Which team is awarded the scrum and where?
drills.notes: The five-metre mark is shown, but six-player scrum engagement is intentionally not animated in this held-up decision lesson.

frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Carrier enters in goal
frames.notes: A1 reaches the in-goal area with possession.

frames.name: Held up · no grounding
frames.notes: PAUSE: the ball never touches the ground.

frames.name: Attacking five-metre scrum

drills.title: Understand the game · U10 no kicking or hand-off
drills.objective: Recognise two U10 restrictions and choose a legal passing option.
drills.players: Blue A = attack towards top; Orange D = defence towards bottom.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones and clear practice grid.
drills.instructions: Pause as D1 closes the space. Ask if A1 may kick or fend. Find A2 behind the ball and replay the legal backward pass.
drills.coaching: U10 does not allow kicking in general play or hand-offs/fending. Use space and a backward pass instead.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration only. Use qualified coaching for any contact or ground technique, and keep enough space.
drills.regression: Set out positions with cones and talk through the correct choice before playing the animation.
drills.progression: Swap the roles or the direction of attack and ask children to explain the correct decision without prompting.
drills.questions: May A1 kick? May A1 fend D1 away? Where is the legal passing option?
drills.notes: The forbidden actions are questions, not movements to imitate. The picture only animates the legal pass and carry.

frames.name: Set up
frames.notes: Identify the ball carrier and direction of attack.

frames.name: Defender closes
frames.notes: D1 moves closer to A1. Ask the group to spot the possible legal passing option to A2.

frames.name: PAUSE · choose the legal option
frames.notes: No kick or hand-off at U10. A2 offers depth.

frames.name: Pass backwards
frames.notes: The ball travels backwards from A1 to A2 instead of being kicked or fended through the defence.

frames.name: Continue playing
frames.notes: A2 accelerates only after receiving the ball. The original carrier can then act as support.

drills.title: Defensive line · Whistle then advance together
drills.objective: Build the simplest defensive-line reaction: on a coach's whistle all six U10 defenders move two short steps forward together, preserve their spacing, then hold their shape. Use this before the carry-or-pass decision drill.
drills.safety: Non-contact reaction drill. Keep a clear run-off and stop the line well before the coach or attacker. The whistle is a coach's practice cue, not a substitute for checking current RFU U10 offside and restart requirements. Never treat this as permission to rush a free pass from an illegal starting position.

frames.name: Set up · six defenders connected
frames.notes: Six defenders form a line at even spacing. The coach stays in the same position as in the later carry-or-pass drill. Explain: react to the whistle together, then stop square and balanced. The attacker and ground ball stay still.

frames.name: Whistle · advance two short steps together
frames.notes: The coach blows the whistle. All six defenders step forward immediately and in unison, without sprinting into contact. Eyes up, spacing unchanged. They must be legally onside before moving in a real restart.

frames.name: Hold shape · look and communicate
frames.notes: Pause and check that the line is still connected, everyone is facing the play and nobody has sprinted out alone. Repeat several times before adding a ball-carrier decision.

drills.players: Six defenders (D1–D6), one support attacker (A1), one coach/ball feeder. Start with all six defenders across the same line. The coach and A1 are behind them, with A1 slightly deeper to receive.
drills.equipment: One rugby ball and four cones to mark an 11 × 20 m working area. No contact pads are required for the touch version.
drills.instructions: 1. Set out the six-defender line as shown. Coach and supporting runner remain in their starting positions. 2. Explain that this is a whistle-reaction exercise, not permission to cross an offside line. 3. Blow the whistle and ask every defender to advance two short steps together. 4. Stop, check spacing and communication, reset, then repeat. 5. Progress to Hold the line · Carry or pass? after the group can move together.
drills.coaching: Coach the timing of the FIRST step, not an all-out sprint. Keep shoulders square, communication short and the line connected. Use the pause to ask who moved early or late. Keep all actions non-contact. At a real U10 free pass, ensure the defenders have retired the required distance and only advance when lawfully permitted.
drills.regression: Start with slower calls and two small steps. Stop if any defender sprints ahead or loses spacing.
drills.progression: Next: Hold the line · Carry or pass? (seed-133). The same defensive line and coach position now develop into two decision outcomes.
drills.questions: Did all six move on the whistle together? Was there a gap after the first step? Can you say which teammate you must stay connected with?
drills.notes: This is the introductory, linear whistle-and-advance drill, not a branching decision. Play it before Hold the line · Carry or pass? to teach the same connected line and short first step. The whistle is a coaching cue; defenders must respect age-grade offside and restart rules in a real game.
